name: Spondylometaphyseal Dysplasia, A4 Type

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Spondylometaphyseal Dysplasia A4 Type

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic vertebral anomalies including platyspondyly and irregular endplates
Metaphyseal irregularities and cupping predominantly affecting long bones
Short stature with disproportionate limb shortening and mild joint laxity
Identification of pathogenic variants in associated gene(s) if available

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: characteristic vertebral anomalies, metaphyseal dysplasia, and clinical features of disproportionate short stature
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation is supportive but not mandatory for diagnosis due to limited data on causative genes.

imaging: Radiographs showing platyspondyly with irregular vertebral endplates
Metaphyseal irregularities and cupping in long bones
Possible thoracic cage deformities on chest X-ray
genetic: Potential pathogenic variants in genes associated with spondylometaphyseal dysplasias (specific gene not well established)
other: Clinical assessment revealing disproportionate short stature and joint laxity

distinguishingFeatures: More pronounced metaphyseal abnormalities with corner fractures
Distinct facial features and more severe spinal involvement

redFlags: Progressive neurological deficits indicating spinal cord compression
Severe respiratory compromise due to thoracic deformity
Rapidly worsening skeletal deformities affecting mobility
references: Superti-Furga A, Unger S. Nosology and classification of genetic skeletal disorders: 2019 revision. Am J Med Genet A. 2019.
Orphanet: Spondylometaphyseal dysplasia, A4 type. ORPHA:168555.
Bonafe L, Cormier-Daire V, Hall C, et al. Nosology and classification of genetic skeletal disorders: 2015 revision. Am J Med Genet A. 2015.
